source.repository: external: numpy/numpy (https://github.com/numpy/numpy), cloned locally for this review

groundTruth.description: A recent (2026) non-security correctness fix in numpy's native StringDType (PR #31662): NpyString_cmp compared string contents with strncmp(), which stops comparing at the first embedded NUL byte in either operand. Since numpy's native string type explicitly supports embedded NUL bytes (unlike C strings), two distinct strings that share a common prefix up to their first NUL byte compared as equal, silently corrupting equality, ordering, sort, and searchsorted results for any such strings. The fix is a one-line change from strncmp to memcmp, plus a doc-comment correction and a new embedded-NUL regression test suite. Second corpus case in C (after case 016), second non-security correctness case (after 008/014), and the second case where the defect lived in a specific function whose doc comment explicitly promised C-strcmp semantics - a useful comment/implementation mismatch of the same shape as case 013's finding-2.

evidence.note: strncmp replaced by memcmp in NpyString_cmp
doc comment corrected from 'same semantics as strcmp on null-terminated C strings' to 'compare using all bytes'
